notes.claim: REQ-03-009 needs a bound the design system's DateRangePicker cannot express, and the bundle's DS-gaps table records only three custom properties while asserting that every new value is one of them

witness.detail: REQ-03-009: 'WHILE the Range window is active and a start has been armed, THE SYSTEM SHALL bound the picker so that no end more than 91 days after that start can be chosen.' In packages/ds/src/components/forms/DateRangePicker.tsx the armed start is private state (`const [pending, setPending] = React.useState<CalendarDate | null>(null)`, :87) and the selectable set is computed from the fixed props alone (`weeks.flat().filter(date => !!date && (!minDate || date >= minDate) && (!maxDate || date <= maxDate))`, :124-127). No prop narrows the panel after the first click, so the requirement cannot be met without changing the component. The cases file's DS gaps table lists only `--name-col`, `--day-col-min`, `--range-label-col` and the three band colours, and closes with 'No colour is written that the design system does not name, and this spec declares no @literal value: every new number is one of the three custom properties above' — which is true of the numbers and silent about the capability.

notes.suggestedFix: a DS-gaps row for the span bound. Planned as T4 regardless: one optional `maxSpanDays` prop on the component, narrowing `availableDates` only — never the minDate/maxDate that gate Calendar's month arrows — and undefined by default so the three shipped report consumers are unchanged.

notes.claim: the DS-gaps table asks for a new custom property to reserve the range label's width, and that reservation already ships under another name

witness.detail: The cases file: '`--range-label-col` — no token carries a reserved width for a variable-width label in a control row | REQ-03-015 needs one.' apps/web/app/globals.css:872-878 already declares `--range-col: 26ch` on the `.time-off-calendar` block and :886-893 applies `width: var(--range-col)` to `.time-off-calendar-range`, added by commit 595fcf6 ('fix(time-off): reserve calendar range label width so nav controls hold still (BUG-013)'), which landed after the bundle was written in e659a5b. Declaring a second property would leave two names reserving one width.

notes.suggestedFix: T5 widens the existing `--range-col` to cover the widest label the four windows now produce and records the decision in the block comment, rather than declaring a second property. The widest string the contracts file names, `28 Dec 2026 – 14 Mar 2027`, is the same length as the widest preset label BUG-013 measured.

notes.rule: contracts §Validation Rules — "The client re-runs rules 1–4 before spending a request"
notes.claim: the screen re-runs none of Validation Rules 1–4, and REQ-03-009's bound is forward-only, so a reader can now build an over-92-day span from the control and spend the request on it

witness.detail: Statement one — contracts.md §Validation Rules, closing paragraph: "The client re-runs rules 1–4 before spending a request; the server re-validates all seven". Statement two — contracts.md §Edge Cases row 7: "A custom range of 93 days, submitted by a client that ignores REQ-03-009 | `422` `rangeTooWide`", which reads as the answer for a NON-compliant client. The code satisfies neither reading: `load` (CalendarScreen.tsx:229-276) never calls `validateTimeOffCalendarRange`, and DateRangePicker.tsx:145 excludes only dates AFTER the armed start, so arming 2026-09-01, paging back and clicking 2026-01-01 commits `[2026-01-01, 2026-09-01]` through commit()'s sort (DateRangePicker.tsx:155-158) — a 244-day span, spent, and answered 422 rangeTooWide. The outcome the reader sees is a message this bundle tabulates, so nothing is broken; what is undecided is whether the compliant client owes a pre-check. REQ-03-009's own heading says "the invalid span is unreachable" while its body and the §UI Description row bound only days after the start, and a reviewer does not settle that.

notes.suggestedFix: Decide it in the document: either the screen owes a span check before the fetch (and the backwards pick is refused client-side), or Edge case 7 is the whole rule and the "client re-runs rules 1–4" sentence does not describe this screen.

notes.rule: reviewer — a fixture whose doc comment claims a safety it does not have
notes.claim: the default `prefix` makes a second call inside one test collide on the unique email column, which is the opposite of what the doc comment promises

witness.detail: `prefix` defaults to `'seeded'` (line 42) and each email is `${prefix}-${index}@seed.test` (line 47) — namespaced by position only, not by organization or by call. A test that seeds an over-cap organization twice, which is exactly what Edge case 1's People-scope mirror would need, throws a Prisma unique-constraint error on `seeded-0@seed.test` on the second call instead of seeding. The doc comment at lines 30-32 states "two calls inside one test do not collide on the unique email column", which holds only if the caller remembers a distinct prefix and the comment does not say so. Nothing fails today: the one call site is apps/api/test/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:1300.

notes.suggestedFix: Fold a per-call token into the email — a module counter or `randomUUID().slice(0, 8)` — so the default is safe, or narrow the comment to say the prefix is the caller's job.
